**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement already contains a workable post-termination transition and records-return regime, which sits at or above our fallback:

- **§ 7.5(a)** – outgoing Servicer must cooperate in an orderly transition of its rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer.
- **§ 7.5(b)** – as soon as practicable after the effective date of resignation/termination, it must transfer all funds relating to the Receivables and **deliver the Receivable Files and the accounts and records it maintains**.
- **§ 7.5(c)** – all reasonable transition expenses of the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and Successor Servicer are **paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer** — better than our preferred "then-current rates" position.
- **§ 7.3** – Cellco must continue performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement, plus continuing remittance obligations under § 3.12(b), so assistance far exceeds 90 days/6 months.
- **§ 3.10(f)** – on termination of the custodial appointment, the Custodian must deliver the Receivable Files to the Indenture Trustee or successor custodian, again at the terminated custodian's cost.

Walk-away territory (no data return, or immediate deletion) is absent. Minor gaps noted for the file only, not redlined: delivery is "as soon as practicable" rather than a hard 30-day outside date; there is no deletion/certification mechanic (appropriate here, since Cellco continues as Marketing Agent/Administrator and needs Obligor data to bill the underlying accounts); and § 7.5(b) carves out proprietary servicing software/models and privacy-restricted material. We would raise the 30-day delivery deadline only as a low-priority comment if the document is otherwise being reopened.
